name: publicWeb_getChatThreads
description: The app's chat thread list for a web member (E9.F7.S15): every run, kennel, room and direct-message thread the member can see, with its unread badge and message count — HC6.hcapp_getEventBadgeCount in its list mode, the same rows the app's Unseen Chats list and the chat bubbles on the run cards read. Wraps the app SP (EXEC) after emitting its own envelope carrying the caller's PublicHasherId (Me). Auth: the wrapped SP's HC6.ValidateAppAuth — the token is signed for hcapp_getEventBadgeCount; the wrapper itself checks nothing before resolving Me from HC.Device.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The browser's HC.Device id (the web member session). No SQL default.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token signed for hcapp_getEventBadgeCount (the SP that validates it). No SQL default.

rowsets.name: WrapperEnvelope
rowsets.description: Always first (unless the Me lookup itself throws): the wrapper's own success envelope with the caller's public id.

columns.name: success
columns.description: Always 1 here.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: Always NULL.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: Always NULL.

columns.name: Me
columns.description: UPPER(CAST(Hasher.PublicHasherId AS NVARCHAR(40))) of the device's hasher, so the web can mark its own messages; NULL when @deviceId matches no live device (the wrapped SP's auth then fails at index 1).

rowsets.name: AuthError
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_getEventBadgeCount (list mode: @publicEventId NULL, @resetBadgeCount 0, @resetAllBadgeCounts 0): Returned on auth failure (invalid token, unrecognised device, etc). errorType=11.

columns.name: errorId
columns.description: HC.ErrorLog GUID for this error.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: Error classification code. 11=auth.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: Numeric error code from ValidateAppAuth.

columns.name: errorTitle
columns.description: Short error title.

columns.name: errorUserMessage
columns.description: User-facing error message.

columns.name: errorProc
columns.description: SP name via OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID).

rowsets.name: AllEventBadgeCounts
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_getEventBadgeCount (list mode: @publicEventId NULL, @resetBadgeCount 0, @resetAllBadgeCounts 0): Returned when @publicEventId is NULL and @resetAllBadgeCounts=0. v1.1.0 (2026-08-28): one row per RUN thread with ANY messages that the user can see — any event they hold a badge row for (posted/read, not time-bounded) OR an event in a kennel they have an HKM row for / an event they have an HEM row for, starting within the last 90 days or in the future — UNION one row per followed kennel-level thread with ANY messages. BadgeCount may be 0. Both thread kinds surface as unread BEFORE first read (no badge row => every message unread). BadgeCount is forced to 0 when the user's effective notification preference for the thread is ignore (2): runs use COALESCE(NULLIF(hem.EventNotificationPreference,0), hkm.KennelNotificationPreference, 0), kennels use hkm.KennelNotificationPreference. Silver Bell (mute=3) still badges. Kennel-thread rows have EventId/PublicEventId NULL and carry PublicKennelId. MessageCount lets the run/kennel cards distinguish unread / read / no-chats. Carries enough fields for the app to render the Unseen Chats list even when the event isn't locally synced (the app filters that list on BadgeCount > 0). First two columns (BadgeCount, PublicEventId) unchanged for back-compat. Previously (v1.0.0) only rows with BadgeCount > 0 were returned. Rows come from HC6.UserUnreadChatThreads(@userId); direct-message rows (ThreadId set) are included only for phones with BuildNumber >= HC6.MinBuildForDmPush() or for a browser (IsMobile = 0), and OtherHasherId is NULL for a browser (lines 313-325).

columns.name: BadgeCount
columns.description: MAX(MessageSequenceCount) - COALESCE(LastSequenceCount, 0), or 0 when the effective notification preference for the thread is ignore (2). 0 = fully read or notifications ignored.

columns.name: PublicEventId
columns.description: The event's public UUID. NULL for kennel-thread rows.

columns.name: EventId
columns.description: HC.Event.id — used to open the chat (ChatPage needs eventId + publicEventId). NULL for kennel-thread rows.

columns.name: EventName
columns.description: HC.Event.EventName for run rows; NULL for kennel, room and DM rows.

columns.name: EventNumber
columns.description: HC.Event.EventNumber.

columns.name: EventStartDatetimeGmt
columns.description: HC.Event.EventStartDatetimeGmt — reliable instant for display/sort.

columns.name: EventImage
columns.description: HC.Event.EventImage (event artwork).

columns.name: KennelId
columns.description: HC.Event.KennelId (run rows) / HC.Kennel.id (kennel rows); NULL for room and DM rows.

columns.name: PublicKennelId
columns.description: HC.Kennel.PublicKennelId for kennel-thread rows; NULL for event rows.

columns.name: KennelShortName
columns.description: HC.Kennel.KennelShortName; NULL for room and DM rows.

columns.name: KennelLogo
columns.description: HC.Kennel.KennelLogo (may be 'bundle://defaultKennelLogo'); NULL for room and DM rows.

columns.name: MessageCount
columns.description: Total non-removed messages in the thread (always > 0 — threads with no messages produce no row). Added v1.1.0.

columns.name: LastMessageAt
columns.description: When the thread last had a message (a DM with none: when the friendship began).

columns.name: Pinned
columns.description: The hasher's own pin (E9.F1.S8 / S25).

columns.name: RoomType
columns.description: Platform-wide room (rooms only).

columns.name: RoomIcon
columns.description: The room's coin art (rooms only).

columns.name: ThreadId
columns.description: Direct-message thread (DMs only; builds >= HC6.MinBuildForDmPush and browsers).

columns.name: OtherPublicHasherId
columns.description: DMs only: the other hasher's public id.

columns.name: OtherDisplayName
columns.description: DMs only: the other hasher's display name.

columns.name: OtherPhoto
columns.description: DMs only: the other hasher's photo.

columns.name: OtherHasherId
columns.description: DMs only: the other hasher's INTERNAL id, for the phone's hasher lists (E9.F1.S32, 2026-10-12). NULL for a browser.

rowsets.name: UnhandledErrorTail
rowsets.description: CATCH path: appended after whatever rowsets were already sent (the success envelope at least, so its position varies — find it by success = 0 / errorCode 1500): { success = 0, errorCode = 1500, errorType = 5 }. No StandardErrorResult follows and the error is not re-raised. The wrapped SPs log and THROW, so this row follows any failure inside them.

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.hcapp_getEventBadgeCount (list mode, no reset) — read-only in that mode.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog ('<web>', userId NULL) in the CATCH, then the 1500 tail row (the error is not re-raised).

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId and @accessToken have no SQL default (line 14). A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default'). The Next.js client always sends them, so this is latent.

codeSmells.issue: Success envelope sent before the work
codeSmells.detail: Rowset 0 { success = 1 } is SELECTed before the wrapped SP runs. When the wrapped SP fails auth its StandardErrorResult arrives at index 1 after a success envelope, and when it THROWs the CATCH appends { success = 0, 1500, 5 } after the success row — so a client reading rowset 0 alone sees success on every call. The web must look for errorId / the trailing row by column name.

Lines 21-24 read the hasher's PublicHasherId from @deviceId alone, before any token check. It is returned in the envelope even when the token is bad — a device id is enough to learn which public hasher id it belongs to.
hcapp_getEventBadgeCount logs and THROWs; the wrapper's CATCH (lines 32-37) logs a second HC.ErrorLog row for the same failure.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
